summary.headline: NAM India posted record FY26 PAT of INR 15.29 bn (+19% YoY) and record quarterly operating profit of INR 4.93 bn (+39% YoY) in Q4 FY26.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was a record operating profit quarter for Nippon Life India AMC, with revenue of INR 7.39 bn (+30% YoY) despite a 14.5% QoQ fall in the Nifty. Mutual fund QAAUM grew 30.1% YoY to INR 7.25 trn and market share rose to 8.89%, its highest since June 2019. Profit after tax of INR 3.85 bn was down 5% QoQ, mainly due to negative other income and a lower tax rate. Management flagged flattening industry SIP net inflows, a pass-through SEBI regulation impact of 3.5-4 bps on equity AUM from April 1, and a proposed SIF launch that is not yet live.

financial_highlights.change: Lower YoY and QoQ due to market volatility

financial_highlights.value: INR 21.50 (~91.5% of net profit), incl. final INR 12.50

segments.name: Mutual fund
segments.commentary: QAAUM INR 7.25 trn, +30.1% YoY and +3.4% QoQ; market share 8.89% (+63 bps YoY, +24 bps QoQ); equity market share 7.16%. MF is about 92% of Q4 revenue and 91% for FY26.

segments.name: ETF
segments.commentary: AUM INR 2.42 trn with 21.40% market share (+234 bps YoY, +109 bps QoQ); 45% share of industry ETF folios. Gold and silver ETFs had combined AUM of about INR 848 bn, up 23% QoQ.

segments.name: AIF
segments.commentary: Cumulative commitments INR 93.3 bn, up 26% YoY; INR 4 bn raised in Q4. NICO 2 first close done, drawn down 25%.

segments.name: Offshore and GIFT City
segments.commentary: Offshore AUM INR 139 bn. GIFT City feeder funds AUM USD 38 mn across two funds.

guidance_outlook: Overall operating expenses guided at around 15-16% YoY growth excluding ESOP, with operating leverage expected as AUM grows.
ESOP cost: Q4 FY26 INR 11 crore; FY26 about INR 43 crore; new plan about INR 35 crore in the next year and INR 70-75 crore over 4 years.
SEBI regulation effective April 1 is expected to impact equity AUM by about 3.5-4 bps; the full cost will be passed through to distributors.
Management says profit growth in absolute terms, not margin bps, is the focus; EBITDA margin is being held despite the lower TER trajectory.
capex_capacity: SIF (Specialised Investment Fund) not yet formally launched; product design and backtesting are underway under industry veteran Andrew.
Fundraising underway for two Listed Equity AIFs, one Private Credit fund and a Direct VC fund.
Non-binding agreement signed for an AIF joint venture to access overseas money in alternatives and infrastructure, and European access via DWS.
Two debt index fund NFOs completed in Q4 raising about INR 8.6 bn cumulatively.
demand_pricing: Industry SIP contribution INR 929 bn in Q4 (+19% YoY, +3% QoQ); March 2026 monthly SIP flows INR 321 bn, an all-time high.
Company monthly systematic book INR 37.2 bn in March 2026 (+17% YoY), annualised INR 447 bn; SIP market share 9.84% in March vs 9.82% in December.
Digital purchase transactions and new SIP registrations 5.04 mn in Q4 (+44% YoY); digital was 77% of new purchase transactions.
Equity and hybrid net sales market share in the high single digits; about double digits excluding NFOs.
Equity yield 53 bps (55 bps ex-arbitrage), debt 25 bps, liquid around 11-12 bps, ETF slightly above 25 bps; blended yield marginally up QoQ on asset mix.
Industry ETF net inflows INR 709 bn (+36% QoQ); company ETF folio share fell from 53% (Q4 FY25) to 45%, which management attributed to commodity-ETF competition rather than share loss in volumes.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the yield increase, and what are yields by category including ETF?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the change is mainly asset mix; equity yield 53 bps (55 bps ex-arbitrage), debt 25 bps, liquid 11-12 bps, ETF slightly above 25 bps; blended yield marginally up QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: How should SIP flows (about INR 3,600-3,700 mn a month) and ESOP costs be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry SIP net inflows have flattened; company is building SIP books in hybrids and commodity funds, with Flexi Cap and sector funds as focus gaps. SIP book share exceeds equity AUM share. ESOP: INR 35 crore next year, INR 70-75 crore over 4 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the April 1 SEBI regulation, and how is it being mitigated?
qa_highlights.answer: Impact about 3.5-4 bps on equity AUM; the full amount is passed through to distributors.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Q4 tax rate low?
qa_highlights.answer: A release after assessments was reversed in Q4, and mark-to-market losses attract lower tax rates.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ETF folio share fall to 45% from 53%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to investors diversifying into commodity ETFs, not competition; the company still leads on volumes and net inflows.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for gold and silver ETF traction, and for expense growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold and silver volumes fell in the last two months as prices dropped, but on Akshaya Tritiya Nippon commodity ETFs took 63% of exchange volume. Expense guidance stays at 15-16% YoY ex-ESOP.

qa_highlights.question: When will SIF launch, and what is its outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Not yet launched; product design and backtesting underway; the management sees it as a long-term pillar but has not put numbers to AUM.

risks_watch: Flattening industry SIP net inflows and high SIP discontinuation in Fintech-sourced SIPs during volatility.
Declining ETF folio share (53% to 45%) and rising competition in commodity ETFs; gold and silver volumes have dipped in the last two months.
SEBI regulation impact of 3.5-4 bps on equity AUM from April 1, 2026, passed through to distributors.
Unresolved SEBI fine overhang; management has nothing new to disclose.
Q4 profit dipped QoQ on lower other income and tax effects; operating margin lower than peers due to ETF mix (33% of AUM).
summary.management_tone: Confident on market share, profit records and the growth pipeline (SIF, AIF, GIFT City), but guarded on near-term SIP and commodity ETF flows. Management deflected the SEBI fine question with no new disclosure.
key_quotes: Our market share at 8.89% is our highest since June 2019.
We are humbled to have over 1 in 3 mutual fund investors invest with us.
The idea is always that we should have an operating leverage and as the AUM grows, the operating leverage should kick in and should help us to reduce the basis over longer period.
So, absolute profit will be more critical for us to monitor and grow as a business.

growth.why: Management guided only opex growth of 15-16% YoY ex-ESOP and "slightly better net sales growth" from SIP-driven share gains, with no quantified revenue guidance; SIP net inflows have flattened and the SIF is not yet launched, so backing is vague.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says it is holding EBITDA margin despite lower TER trajectory, focus is absolute profit growth not margin bps; SEBI 3.5-4 bps equity AUM impact from April 1 is passed through to distributors, and opex guided at 15-16% YoY ex-ESOP.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: QAAUM up 30.1% YoY to INR 7.25 trn with market share 8.89% (highest since June 2019) and company monthly systematic book INR 37.2 bn in March (+17% YoY); management guides to slightly better net sales growth, but industry SIP net inflows have flattened and gold/silver ETF volumes dipped in last two months.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No quantified revenue or margin guidance raise; only opex growth of 15-16% YoY ex-ESOP held and 'slightly better net sales growth' stated, with SIP inflows flattening.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: SIP net inflows flattening industry-wide, ETF folio share down from 53% to 45%, and a 3.5-4 bps equity AUM hit from April 1 SEBI rule could pressure revenue, though guidance is held at 15-16% opex growth.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: SIF not yet launched (product design and backtesting underway), with two Listed Equity AIFs, one Private Credit fund and a Direct VC fund in fundraising, and two debt index NFOs raised about INR 8.6 bn in Q4.

rows.label: AIF JV for overseas money and DWS European access
rows.why: Non-binding agreement signed for an AIF joint venture to access overseas money in alternatives and infrastructure, with AIF cumulative commitments at INR 93.3 bn (+26% YoY) and INR 4 bn raised in Q4.

rows.label: Company monthly systematic book growth
rows.why: Monthly systematic book INR 37.2 bn in March 2026 (+17% YoY), annualised INR 447 bn, with SIP market share 9.84% in March vs 9.82% in December.

rows.label: Unresolved SEBI fine overhang
rows.why: Management deflected the SEBI fine question with nothing new to disclose, leaving the outcome and timing open.

tone.note: Management was confident on market share (8.89%), record profits and the SIF/AIF/GIFT City pipeline but cautious on SIP flattening and commodity ETF flows; analysts pushed on yields, ESOP cost, SEBI regulation impact and the ETF folio share fall, and management deflected the SEBI fine question.
